questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Enhancing French language skills/mastery.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language, philosophical tradition and the history of the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly complicated and not very transparent. We found our way but it required a lot of time and grit. And oftentimes emails or meetings back and forth between students and administrators.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a very general introductory meeting with the administration and student initiatives for international students. Other than that our more specific coordinator within each our respective disciplines were available for meetings or mail correspondances.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The system around finding and gaining acces to course could be much more transparent and less rigid. Also in terms of informing the students of what they can possibly do and not do. As it is now it an unecessarily timeconsuming affair for everyone involved.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly hard and required a lot of time, grit and speedy decisions. A recommendation could be to start renting a temporary place for a month and then finding something more "permanent" when you are there. It is much easier to find accomodation, while you are in the city and have the opportunity to visit places.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do it! But be prepared and start looking in good time. You will also need almost every imaginable document to get a flat in France, specially Paris. It is not an easy task, but worth it once you are there and have found a place. The city is magnifique.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not transparent at all. Very difficult to follow, gain insight and overview over your possibilities as a student.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A lot of different brochures with no timetables attached to them, which you then needed to cross check with all your chosen interesting courses, making a huge puzzle. Even there, you couldn't be certain that you were allowed to choose these courses, why you needed to prepare several scenarios and possibilities. Other than that, there was a lot of confusion over the form and timing of exam, which made planning and prioritization of energy and focus very difficult for at least half of the duration of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Brochures. After the start of the semester, the coordinator only answered emails sporadically and some not at all.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Partially.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare as well as you can. Read everything relevant in all of the available and relevant brochures and most importantly: be patient with the administration and the process related. It is not your fault and you should not let yourself be too occupied with tardiness and lack of organisation and cooperation. Once you are through with it, the courses in themselves, the content, the teaching and the engagement of the students is awesome.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very high level academically, especially in the courses in French.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Especially the courses at the Philosophy of Art and Political Philosophy programmes were of a very high level academically. The frame of reference and the demands of historical and contemporary knowledge was quite high and a prerequisite for keeping up and being able to think with the content, questions and thoughts of the course and the lecturer. Incredibly inspiring, inticing and stimulating.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More strictly lectures. Not a lot of debate between students and lecturer. There was some, but not a lot. Also there were no breaks every 15 minutes. Lectures are one-and-a-half to two hours straight.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Les figures de la répétition (Philosophie de l'art)
2) Esthétique environnementale (Philosophie de l'art)
3) Séminaire Centre Victor Basch (Philosophie de l'art)
4) Démocratie et écologie (Philosophie politique)
5) Éthique environnmentale (Philosophie politique)
6) Philosophy of Biology (Philosophie de sciences)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
1) Les figures de la répétition (Philosophie de l'art) -- Inspiring teacher and continental philosophy readings.
2) Esthétique environnementale (Philosophie de l'art) -- Interesting history of the coming into existence of "paysage", both understood as the landscape itself and the painting of same form/representation
4) Démocratie et écologie (Philosophie politique) -- Provocative, radical and progressive course, where we were allowed to doubt, critize and suggest ameliorations liberal representative democraties in the light of climate, biodiversity and environmental crises.
&
6) Philosophy of Biology (Philosophie de sciences) -- Interesting to dwell upon the assimilation of the phenomenon of life into the sciences and discover, that we do not have a clear way of distinguishing neither life itself, nor organisms, nor species. We are living in a fragmental science fiction!

questions.answer: Food was less expensive, rent was a bit more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, movie clubs, talking cafés in French and others.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The movie club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The old cinemas in Saint Germain des Prés. All the musuems that might interest you (there are too many for one semester, so get going!). Both traditional and modern French cuisines.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have lived there before, seven years ago, so I found fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be kind and try striking up conversation in their mother tongue.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The competitiveness.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Le savoir-vivre.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Learn French as well as you can before going.
2) Be prepared to work, read, write and do it all in a new way/tradition/method.
3) Surrender yourself to the culture and ways of doing things at the university and take it as a learning and an experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to find stable housing in the Eastern part of Paris. You will not regret it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Producing the assignments and oral presentations through out the semester as well as exploring the city, culture and traditions within.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding my way through course selection and administration issues.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
